strengths: The paper presents a useful Algorithms/General contribution: learned spatial compression makes joint diffusion over VAE latents and VFM semantics substantially more effective. The formulation is technically coherent, and channel-wise fusion preserves the patch-token sequence length, making the approach practical.

Matched-budget results support the main empirical contribution. At 400K steps, SiT-B/2 improves from 21.4 FID with ReDi and 15.2 with REG to 12.9 with REGLUE. Improvements also hold for SiT-XL/2, including 3.2 versus REG’s 3.4 at 400K steps and 2.5 versus 2.7 at 1M steps.

Table 1 provides informative component ablations: learned local semantics alone achieve 14.3 FID, multi-layer aggregation improves this to 13.3, and the complete combination reaches 12.9. These results substantiate the emphasis on local semantic modeling rather than attributing all gains to the combined system.

The experimental analysis extends beyond headline FID: compressor width, channel count, layer selection, auxiliary objectives, alternative VFMs, unconditional generation, and limited-data settings are examined. Classification and Cityscapes segmentation probes provide additional evidence that the compressed representations preserve useful semantic information.

The manuscript clearly attributes its relationship to REPA, ReDi, and REG, supplies substantial implementation details, and appropriately acknowledges limits on resolution and training duration. Acceptance does not depend on outperforming much longer-trained models.
weaknesses: Originality is concentrated in replacing PCA with a convolutional autoencoder and aggregating several VFM layers; joint semantic–latent diffusion, global-token modeling, and external alignment are inherited components. This is a meaningful empirical improvement, but the conceptual advance is narrower than the broad unified-framework framing suggests.

The experiments do not fully isolate nonlinearity as the cause of improvement. The convolutional compressor also introduces spatial mixing and learned feature scaling. A matched spatial linear compressor and a pointwise nonlinear compressor, with controlled normalization and channel counts, would distinguish these effects. The current evidence establishes the effectiveness of the proposed compressor more strongly than the claim that nonlinearity itself is key.

Efficiency is demonstrated primarily through iteration counts. Compressor pretraining is reported as taking under an hour on eight A100s, but matched end-to-end training time, feature-extraction costs, memory, and diffusion throughput are not reported. Table 5 measures compressor throughput rather than complete-system throughput, leaving the practical speedup and essentially unchanged inference-cost claims incompletely verified.

Several complementary gains are small and lack uncertainty estimates: external alignment changes 14.3 to 14.1 FID, the 1M-step XL comparison changes 2.7 to 2.5, and matched 160-epoch guided generation changes 1.59 to 1.53. Repeated runs or evaluation uncertainty would strengthen these specific claims. Generation experiments also remain confined to ImageNet at 256×256, limiting evidence for broader applicability.

Some reporting inconsistencies hinder reproduction and interpretation. Figures 4 and 6 associate 14.3/13.3 FID with 8/16 channels, whereas Table 6 associates those same scores with single-layer/four-layer inputs at 16 channels; these configurations need reconciliation. Semantic-feature normalization and loss-reduction conventions are unspecified despite their relevance to joint diffusion. The abstract’s code-availability statement also contains no visible link.

strengths: As an Algorithms/General contribution, REGLUE offers a technically coherent extension of joint representation–latent diffusion. Its main contribution is learned spatial compression of multi-layer VFM features, integrated with global-token modeling and representation alignment. The manuscript appropriately acknowledges REPA, ReDi, and REG.

The reported improvements support practical value. At 400K steps, SiT-B/2 improves from 21.4 FID with ReDi and 15.2 with REG to 12.9 with REGLUE. SiT-XL/2 reaches REG’s 1M-step FID of 2.7 at 700K steps (Tables 2–3). These gains support a modest preference for acceptance despite the reservations below.

The experimental analysis is substantial: Table 1 separates several semantic signals, while additional experiments examine compressor width, feature dimensionality, layer selection, training objectives, alternative VFMs, unconditional generation, and limited-data settings. ImageNet probing and Cityscapes segmentation provide useful evidence that the compressed features retain semantic information.

The architecture preserves the spatial token count and adds only one global token, making low inference overhead plausible. The appendix supplies useful architecture and optimization details and explicitly acknowledges the limits of training duration and resolution.
weaknesses: Originality is incremental. Local-feature joint diffusion, global-token joint diffusion, and external alignment already come from ReDi, REG, and REPA; the principal new element is a conventional convolutional reconstruction autoencoder applied to selected VFM layers. The scientific case therefore depends primarily on the empirical usefulness and explanation of this design.

The experiments establish that the proposed compressor works better than the tested PCA baseline, but do not fully isolate why. The main comparisons also change feature dimensionality and, in some settings, layer aggregation. The matched 8-channel probing comparison helps, but matched PCA experiments at 16 channels and with the same multi-layer inputs, plus a spatial linear compressor or pointwise nonlinear compressor, would distinguish nonlinearity from spatial mixing and capacity.

The strongest-baseline gains become small at larger scale: XL/2 improves from 3.4 to 3.2 FID at 400K steps and from 2.7 to 2.5 at 1M; with CFG, the 160-epoch gain is 1.59 to 1.53. No repeated-run uncertainty is reported. Likewise, describing the 14.3-to-14.1 alignment gain as consistently beneficial and the components as synergistic is stronger than the available single-run, incomplete factorial evidence supports.

Training acceleration is demonstrated in iterations rather than total compute. The appendix reports compressor training below one hour on eight A100s and approximately seven days for an XL/2 run, but lacks matched end-to-end timings against REG and ReDi that include feature extraction, preprocessing, and storage costs. Table 5 measures compressor throughput, not diffusion training or sampling throughput.

Some reproducibility and reporting details need clarification. Feature normalization and per-modality loss reduction are not specified clearly, although both affect the balance of the joint objective. Appendix A.1 associates 14.3 FID with an 8-channel compressor and 13.3 with 16 channels, whereas Table 6 associates those values with single-layer versus four-layer inputs at 16 channels; the probing configurations need explicit reconciliation. Generation evidence is also confined to ImageNet 256×256 and the SiT family, limiting claims of general applicability.

strengths: As an Algorithms/General contribution, REGLUE offers a useful, technically coherent extension of joint representation–latent diffusion. Learned spatial compression and aggregation of deep VFM features are practical improvements, and the paper appropriately acknowledges REPA, ReDi, and REG.

The gains are substantial on SiT-B/2: at 400K steps, REGLUE achieves 12.9 FID versus 21.4 for ReDi and 15.2 for REG. Improvements also persist on SiT-XL/2, reaching 2.7 FID at 700K steps versus REG’s 2.7 at 1M. These results support the value of the approach without requiring an absolute state-of-the-art score.

The experimental investigation is unusually broad within its benchmark: Table 1 separates several semantic signals, while further experiments examine compressor capacity, feature layers, training objectives, guidance, alternative VFMs, unconditional generation, and limited-data settings. Classification and segmentation probes provide additional evidence that the compressor retains useful semantics.

The architecture preserves the spatial token count and adds only one global token, making the improvement attractive for existing SiT pipelines. The appendix provides substantial architecture and optimization details and candidly identifies the limits of the training budget and resolution.
weaknesses: The central attribution to nonlinear compression needs cleaner controls. The principal ReDi comparison uses eight PCA channels versus the default sixteen learned channels, and there is no matched sixteen-channel PCA or linear spatial-autoencoder baseline. Figures 4 and 6 include an eight-channel learned variant, but their reported 14.3 FID conflicts with Table 7’s assignment of 14.3 to sixteen-channel, last-layer compression; similarly, 13.3 is associated with multi-layer input in Table 6. These inconsistencies should be resolved to establish how much improvement comes from nonlinearity, spatial mixing, dimensionality, and layer aggregation.

The novelty is primarily a well-motivated combination and refinement of existing ideas. Joint semantic–latent diffusion, global-token modeling, and external alignment are inherited components. Moreover, the additional global/alignment benefit is relatively small: Table 1 improves from 13.3 to 12.9 when adding these signals to multi-layer local modeling. The evidence is strongest for the compressor rather than a distinctive global–local synergy.

Several improvements over the strongest baseline are small and lack uncertainty estimates: XL FID improves from 2.7 to 2.5 without guidance, and from 1.59 to 1.53 with guidance at 160 epochs. Repeated runs or uncertainty estimates would strengthen these comparisons and claims that small auxiliary-component gains are consistent.

Iteration savings are demonstrated more clearly than end-to-end compute savings. The appendix reports compressor pretraining below one hour on eight A100s, but does not provide matched diffusion training throughput, inference latency, or total preprocessing costs against REG/ReDi. Similar parameter counts and token counts support low overhead but do not fully establish it.

Generation is evaluated only on ImageNet at 256×256 with SiT backbones, limiting evidence for broader applicability. Reproduction also requires clarification of semantic-feature normalization and loss reduction across modalities; these affect the effective noise scales and objective weights. The abstract’s claimed code link is blank in the supplied manuscript.

strengths: The paper makes a useful Algorithms/General contribution: learned spatial compression of multi-layer VFM features improves joint image–feature diffusion, while channel-wise fusion preserves the backbone’s token count. The method is technically coherent and clearly positioned relative to REPA, ReDi, and REG.

The main empirical gains are substantial. At 400K steps, SiT-B/2 improves from 21.4 FID with ReDi and 15.2 with REG to 12.9. At XL scale, REGLUE matches REG’s 1M-step FID of 2.7 at 700K steps. Table 13 supports the efficiency claim with compute accounting, beyond iteration counts alone.

The ablations are unusually extensive: Table 1 separates local semantics, global semantics, alignment, and multi-layer aggregation; further experiments examine compression width, capacity, feature layers, regularization, and fusion. Learned local compression alone achieves 14.3 FID, supporting its importance independently of the complete framework.

The supplementary evidence broadens the case through Food-101, ImageNet-512, unconditional generation, limited-data experiments, alternative quality metrics, and semantic probing. These results support practical value beyond one headline FID, and the limitations discussion appropriately acknowledges untested large-scale regimes.
weaknesses: The conceptual novelty is concentrated in the learned compressor and its integration. Joint spatial-feature diffusion, global-token diffusion, and external alignment come from existing methods. The contribution is a meaningful empirical improvement, but the broader framing of a new unified framework somewhat exceeds the methodological departure.

The evidence does not fully isolate nonlinearity as the decisive mechanism. Relative to PCA, the convolutional autoencoder also introduces spatial mixing and a learned reconstruction mapping. A spatial linear compressor, a pointwise nonlinear compressor, or a controlled smoothing baseline would help distinguish these effects. Figure 3 establishes an association between frequency profiles and FID, rather than demonstrating that high-frequency suppression causes the improvement.

Some compressor results require reconciliation. Figure 2 and supplementary Section A.1 associate 14.3 FID with an 8-channel compressor and 13.3 with 16 channels, whereas Tables 7–8 associate 14.3 with a single-layer, 16-channel compressor and 13.3 with multi-layer compression. The exact feature-layer and channel configurations behind the probing plots are therefore unclear, weakening their interpretation as controlled comparisons.

The smaller improvements lack uncertainty estimates: examples include alignment improving 14.3 to 14.1 FID and REGLUE improving REG from 2.7 to 2.5 at XL scale. Independent runs or uncertainty estimates would better support claims of consistent complementarity. These concerns do not negate the much larger gains over PCA-based compression.

Reproducibility is incomplete despite substantial architecture and optimizer details. The manuscript does not clearly specify semantic-feature normalization/scaling, modality-loss reduction conventions, or the full probing protocols; these matter when jointly diffusing modalities of different dimensions and scales. The abstract’s code-availability statement also has no link. Efficiency wording should distinguish unchanged inference throughput relative to REG from the measurable overhead relative to vanilla SiT.

strengths: Assessed as Algorithms/General, REGLUE makes a useful empirical contribution: learned spatial compression enables effective joint diffusion of local semantics, global semantics, and VAE latents. The formulation is coherent, and the manuscript appropriately attributes its foundations to ReDi, REG, REPA, and SiT.

The improvements are supported across model scales and training budgets. At 400K steps, SiT-B/2 improves from REG's 15.2 FID to 12.9; SiT-XL/2 reaches REG's 1M-step FID of 2.7 at 700K steps. With guidance, the matched-budget improvements from 1.86 to 1.59 and from 1.59 to 1.46 are practically meaningful.

The experimental coverage is substantial. Table 1 separates several semantic inputs and alignment choices, while additional experiments examine compressor capacity, feature layers, dimensionality, fusion, guidance, and alternative VFMs. Supplementary Food-101, ImageNet-512, limited-data, and alternative-metric results strengthen the evidence beyond the primary benchmark.

The efficiency argument has quantitative support: channel-wise fusion preserves the token count relative to REG, and supplementary Table 13 reports compute savings at comparable quality while including VFM and compressor costs. Architectural and optimization details are reasonably extensive, and the limitations section acknowledges untested longer schedules.
weaknesses: The methodological novelty is incremental. Joint feature–image diffusion, global-token modeling, and external alignment come from existing methods; the main new ingredient is a conventional convolutional autoencoder applied to multi-layer VFM features. The paper's value therefore rests primarily on its empirical findings rather than a fundamentally new generative formulation.

The evidence establishes that the proposed compressor works better than the evaluated PCA configurations, but does not isolate nonlinearity as the decisive cause. The compressor also introduces spatial mixing and learned reconstruction. Comparisons against a linear spatial compressor, a pointwise nonlinear compressor, or suitably smoothed PCA features would distinguish these explanations. Figure 3's frequency profiles are suggestive correlations rather than causal evidence for improved diffusability.

Some semantic-preservation results are difficult to reconcile across configurations. Figure 2 and supplementary A.1 associate the 8- and 16-channel compressors with FIDs of approximately 14.3 and 13.3, whereas Table 7 assigns 14.3 to single-layer 16-channel compression and 13.3 to multi-layer 16-channel compression. These plots need explicit layer, alignment, and global-token settings to make their comparisons interpretable.

The smaller complementary gains lack uncertainty estimates. Improvements such as 14.3 to 14.1 from alignment and 2.7 to 2.5 at XL scale are reported without repeated training runs or evaluation uncertainty. Table 1 also changes global modeling and global alignment together in relevant comparisons, limiting attribution of their individual benefits.

Reproducibility and wording need refinement. The abstract's code-availability statement has no link, and normalization or scaling of compressed semantic latents is not clearly specified despite its importance under a shared noise schedule. Claims of unchanged throughput should explicitly use REG as the comparator: Table 2 reports 3.8 images/s for REGLUE versus 4.1 for vanilla SiT. These concerns qualify the claims but do not outweigh the broader empirical case for acceptance.

strengths: The paper presents a useful Algorithms/General contribution: joint diffusion of VAE latents, compressed spatial semantics, and a global semantic token. The formulation is coherent, and channel-wise fusion preserves the patch-token count, making the approach practical without substantially increasing sampling cost.

The improvements are consistent across model scales and training budgets. At 400K steps, SiT-B/2 improves from REG’s 15.2 FID to 12.9; SiT-XL/2 matches REG’s 1M-step FID of 2.7 at 700K steps. Supplementary Table 13 strengthens the convergence claim by reporting compute rather than iterations alone.

The experimental investigation is substantial. Table 1 separates several semantic modeling and alignment choices, while additional experiments examine compression width, feature layers, compressor capacity, alternative VFMs, fusion strategies, and guidance. Nonlinear local modeling alone achieves 14.3 FID, supporting the compressor’s value independently of the complete combination.

Evidence extends beyond a single FID comparison: semantic probing, Cityscapes segmentation, alternative distribution metrics, unconditional generation, Food-101, and ImageNet-512 support the approach’s utility. The paper appropriately attributes its principal building blocks and acknowledges limitations in large-scale, long-schedule evaluation.
weaknesses: The conceptual advance is relatively incremental over ReDi, REG, and REPA: the main new ingredient is a conventional convolutional autoencoder for spatial feature compression, combined with established joint modeling and alignment. The empirical contribution supports acceptance, but the unified formulation itself is less novel than the presentation sometimes suggests.

The claim that nonlinearity is the decisive mechanism is not fully isolated. Compared with PCA, the compressor also introduces spatial mixing and a different learned representation geometry. Although matched-channel comparisons support its effectiveness, a linear spatial compressor, a pointwise nonlinear compressor, or a smoothed-PCA control would better distinguish these explanations. Figure 3 establishes an association between frequency content and generation quality, rather than a causal explanation.

Some improvements central to the claimed complementarity are small and lack uncertainty estimates: alignment changes FID from 14.3 to 14.1, the full configuration improves over multilayer local-only modeling from 13.3 to 12.9, and the XL advantage over REG is 0.2 FID at both 400K and 1M steps. Repeated runs would help establish the reliability of these smaller effects; this concern is less consequential for the larger compressor gains.

Several reporting details need reconciliation for reproducibility. Figure 2 and Supplementary A.1 associate 8/16-channel compression with FIDs of 14.3/13.3, whereas Tables 5 and 7 associate these results differently with channel count and layer selection. The semantic-feature normalization and precise loss reduction across modalities are also unspecified, despite their effect on relative noise and loss scales. Finally, the abstract announces available code but supplies no link. These are correctable issues, but the compression comparisons should be made unambiguous.
